title: Rigveda 10.170: To Surya
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 (1711 CE (colophon: Saṃvat 1768)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 10.170: To Surya: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of a 1711 Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 10.170 is a hymn of 4 verses addressed to Surya. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 10, the last and latest book. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 (University of Pennsylvania), a paper manuscript of the eighth aṣṭaka (RV 10.46-10.191) of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā in Devanāgarī, 158 leaves, 6 lines to the page, with the accents marked in red; the scribe's colophon on fol. 158 gives Saṃvat 1768 (1711 CE); this hymn stands on fol. 147v-148r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Like most Rigveda manuscripts, Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 writes a repeated refrain in short form after its first occurrence (for example kasmai° for kasmai devāya haviṣā vidhema); the Sanskrit shown is the full text of Aufrecht's edition.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).

translation.original_ref: RV 10.170.1-4 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 8, varga 28); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 148r
translation.original_text:
1vi̱bhrāḍ bṛ̱hat pi̍batu so̱myam madhv āyu̱r dadha̍d ya̱jñapa̍tā̱v avi̍hrutam | vāta̍jūto̱ yo a̍bhi̱rakṣa̍ti̱ tmanā̍ pra̱jāḥ pu̍poṣa puru̱dhā vi rā̍jati ||
2vi̱bhrāḍ bṛ̱hat subhṛ̍taṁ vāja̱sāta̍ma̱ṁ dharma̍n di̱vo dha̱ruṇe̍ sa̱tyam arpi̍tam | a̱mi̱tra̱hā vṛ̍tra̱hā da̍syu̱haṁta̍ma̱ṁ jyoti̍r jajñe asura̱hā sa̍patna̱hā ||
3i̱daṁ śreṣṭha̱ṁ jyoti̍ṣā̱ṁ jyoti̍r utta̱maṁ vi̍śva̱jid dha̍na̱jid u̍cyate bṛ̱hat | vi̱śva̱bhrāḍ bhrā̱jo mahi̱ sūryo̍ dṛ̱śa u̱ru pa̍prathe̱ saha̱ ojo̱ acyu̍tam ||
4vi̱bhrāja̱ñ jyoti̍ṣā̱ sva1̱̍r aga̍ccho roca̱naṁ di̱vaḥ | yene̱mā viśvā̱ bhuva̍nā̱ny ābhṛ̍tā vi̱śvaka̍rmaṇā vi̱śvade̍vyāvatā ||
translation.text:
1MAY the Bright God drink glorious Soma-mingled meath, giving the sacrifice's lord uninjured life; He who, wind-urged, in person guards our offspring well, hath nourished them with food and shines o'er many a land.
2Radiant, as high Truth, cherished, best at winning strength, Truth based upon the statute that supports the heavens, He rose, a light, that kills Vr̥itras and enemies, best slayer of the Dasyus, Asuras, and foes.
3This light, the best of lights, supreme, all-conquering, winner of riches, is exalted with high laud. All-lighting, radiant, mighty as the Sun to see, he spreadeth wide unfailing victory and strength.
4Beaming forth splendour with thy light, thou hast attained heaven's lustrous realm. By thee were brought together all existing things, possessor of all Godhead, All-effecting God.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48, fol. 148r (OPenn image 147, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 10.170.1 ‹-yajñapatāv avihrutam›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 148v, begins in RV 10.171.1 ‹aśṛṇoḥ somino havam›. Verses 10.170.1-4 end on this page; 10.170.1 begins on fol. 147v.
